incident-bot: INCIDENT: gpu-prefill-container-restarts detected on cluster-prod-us-west-2. Alert level: P1. Affected service: redwood-runtime. Symptoms: repeated container restarts on inference nodes -> OOM during prefill. Pager escalated to @Ryan (oncall). Link: https://incidents.redwood.example/3971234567

Ryan (oncall): I'm on it. Paging SREs and eng-runtime. Any immediate customer impact?

Liz (support): Getting a handful of realtime alerts from a single customer (edge AI vendor) reporting timeouts and 500s for long prompts since ~07:42 UTC. They've opened a ticket.

Maria (eng-runtime): Seeing container restarts on nodes gpu-uk-3 and gpu-usw2-11. Crash reason in kube events: "OOMKilled" during prefill. Prefill token counts spiking to ~120k for a few requests.

Jordan (SRE): Pulling pod logs now. `kubectl describe pod redwood-runtime-7f9d` shows repeated OOMKilled and restartCount 4. dmesg has: 
```
[  1234.567890] Out of memory: Kill process 23456 (python) score 987 or sacrifice child
[  1234.568000] Killed process 23456 (python) total-vm: 8123456kB, anon-rss: 18000000kB
```

Maria (eng-runtime): stacktrace in runtime logs points to prefill buffer allocation: `kv_cache.allocate(seq_len * embedding_dim * 4)` failing when seq_len >> expectation. Prefetch/cache logic tried to pre-allocate huge prefix KV for long prompt.

Ana (ML): That token count is huge. Looks like a customer sent a concatenated history with lots of embeddings and images->text. Could be prompt construction issue on their side, but runtime should cap allocations.

Ryan (oncall): Mitigation plan: 1) apply emergency runtime config to cap prefill tokens per-request (max_prefill_tokens=65536) 2) enable prefetch fallback (fallback_to_prefix-trim) to drop older context if prefill would exceed threshold 3) scale down affected nodes for now to reduce restarts and route traffic to warm nodes. Who can change the config?

Maria (eng-runtime): I can push a canary config to Dedicated pool and flip on the cap. Preparing a hotfix: runtime PR will add safe-guard and a graceful trim path. Patch ready: `runtime: add prefill_token_cap and safe_trim_policy` — will deploy as canary to two pods first.

Deploy Bot: deploy triggered by Maria: runtime-hotfix/2026-03-15-07:55 -> canary (2 pods). CI passed.

Jordan (SRE): I will cordon gpu-usw2-11 and drain safely to avoid repeated crashes while canary propagates. Running: `kubectl cordon gpu-usw2-11 && kubectl drain gpu-usw2-11 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

Liz (support): Notifying the impacted customer: "We're investigating elevated errors for long prompts; mitigation in progress. We'll follow up with ETA once canary validated." They responded: "Appreciate it — it's urgent, many requests in flight."

Maria (eng-runtime): Canary logs show prefill cap applied; for a request that previously requested 120k tokens, we now log: `prefill_request_trimmed: true, original_tokens:120512, trimmed_to:65536, reason:prefill_token_cap` and the runtime returned truncated response rather than crash. No OOM.

Jordan (SRE): After canary validated for ~6 minutes, rolling patch to rest of pool started. Also enabled "prefetch-cache-fallback" which falls back to partial KV cache and trims oldest entries when allocation > 50% GPU mem budget.

Ryan (oncall): Routing changes: shifted ~30% of traffic off busy nodes to warm pool and increased prefetch timeout to avoid sudden bursts. Monitoring for error rate and latency.

Ana (ML): Quick note — trimmed responses may affect customer quality. Recommend we attach a header in the response `x-prefill-trimmed: true` and track against eval set. Adding to follow-ups.

Liz (support): Updated customer: "We've applied a mitigations patch which prevents crashes but may trim very long inputs; we're monitoring. We'll share a postmortem and permanent fix plan shortly." They replied: "Ok thanks, keep us posted."

Jordan (SRE): After full rollout, node restarts dropped to 0, OOM traces gone. Error rate for the affected endpoint reduced from 12% -> 1.2%. Latency spike subsided.

Maria (eng-runtime): Creating a follow-up issue: runtime #4821: "Safe prefill limits + configurable trim policies + metrics (prefill_trim_count, prefill_trim_tokens)". Also adding an alert for sustained prefill token > 80k per-request.

Ryan (oncall): Summary for incident channel: cause = large prefill allocations from very long prompts causing GPU OOM and container restarts. Mitigation = canary deployment of prefill token cap + prefetch-cache-fallback, draining affected nodes, routing changes. Customer impact = timeouts/500s for one customer for ~18 minutes, degraded quality for very long prompts due to trimming. No data loss.

Ana (ML): Follow-ups: (a) add response header & telemetry (b) add runtime config guardrails + unit tests (c) evaluate heuristic to detect client-side prompt concatenation abuse and provide SDK guidance.

Liz (support): I'll schedule the customer follow-up meeting and include the PR link and incident timeline.

Ryan (oncall): I'll hand off to Maria for postmortem and tag this resolved in pager. If anyone notices regressions, reopen. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: 3971234567. Duration: ~25 minutes. Postmortem link: https://incidents.redwood.example/3971234567/postmortem

Maria (eng-runtime): Adding notes to postmortem and will own the action items. Thanks everyone for quick ops.
